chapter: Los Angeles scene, Tatum and Billy Berg's
title: Singing blues with Art Tatum at Lovejoy's and on Decca
summary: Tatum accompanied Turner at Lovejoy's Big-Legged Chicken, then they recorded for Decca; his name was first left off the label.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: You made those in New York, you said?
In New York. I made some records with Art Tatum in New York. First, I met Art Tatum here in California. He used to play down on Central Avenue.
At Lovejoy's?
At Love...Alec Lovejoy's place called The Big-Legged Chicken. Hahhhh! You remember.
I've heard about it. I was...I was never at Lovejoy's but I just...it was upstairs?
Yeah.
And he used to be there, like every night...
Yeah...yeah...
With his beer beside him...a case of beer beside him while he played. Is that right?
Yeah. Yeah.
And you used to go into Lovejoy's?
Yeah, I used to go up to Lovejoy's.
Did you ever sing with him in there?
That's where I started singing with him at.
Ohh. Ohhhhhhhhhh.

Art Tatum...I walked up to him and asked him, I say, 'You play so much piano,' so I asked him could he play any blues. He say, 'Yeah, can you sing 'em?' So me an' him used to be up there every night, together, bangin' around on the...he be playin' the piano an' I be singin' the blues.
Reel 4
So I went back... We used to hang out together.

So I went back to New York City, an' he came to New York. He was workin' there, an' he had a record date, so he called me up at the hotel and asked me would I come down to the Decca. He wanted me to sing some blues with him on his session.

So I went... I went down there, an' we made four...five sides an' ever'body thought it was Art Tatum singin' on the record so we had to get that straight...'cause you never heard Art Tatum sing. So we got that all straightened out. When the record was out, it was a hit--"Wee Baby Blues"..."Cherry Red" an' all them kind of numbers like that, an' we got that all cooked up, an' ever'body thought that was him singin'.
Well, wasn't...when they first came out, didn't they leave your name off the label or something?
Yeah, then they hadn't my name on it at all. I was just a vocalist.
And how long before they...they got the right kind of label on there?

Well, took 'bout a year or two years. They finally got around...'course, they called me back to do some sessions with Frankie Newton, the band that played down at Cafe Society, an' uh, they called us back down there to do some records with them, so that's when they corrected it...'cause they remembered me from bein' down there before.
